title: Attenuation and Priority Hedging Cookbook
author: Arjun Mehta
content:
Summary:
This cookbook defines a pragmatic, reproducible approach for attenuating service quality and applying priority hedging in Redwood's multi-tenant inference platform. It codifies decision thresholds, telemetry signals, and concrete runbook steps to intentionally reduce non-critical consumption (attenuation) while protecting global SLOs and preserving error budget for critical tenants or system paths.

Why this doc exists:
- Multi-tenant inference workloads can produce high variance in token demand and tail latency.
- When headroom is constrained, abrupt throttling causes customer outages and poor UX.
- Attenuation reduces quality in controlled ways (e.g., model fallback, reduced context, batched responses, rate-limited optional features) to maintain availability for high-priority traffic.

Scope:
- Applies to Redwood-hosted runtime, Dedicated pool leaders, and Private control-plane policies where platform-level attenuation is supported.
- Focus on runtime-level controls (batching/k-v cache eviction, model variant fallback, per-tenant rate shaping) and policy orchestration (priority lists, hedging weights).
- Does NOT replace tenant-specific escape-hatches (customer-configured throttles).

Definitions:
- Attenuation: intentional, reversible reduction of non-essential serving properties to preserve SLOs (examples: shorter max tokens, lower-quality model, payload sampling).
- Priority Hedging: allocating remaining error budget/headroom preferentially to higher-tier tenants or critical routes.
- Critical routes: control-plane, billing, health-checks, token validation, streaming sessions marked 'pinned'.

Service and SLO examples (reference):
- model-serving (public-api): Availability SLO = 99.9% successful-generate per-minute, Latency SLO p99 < 350ms.
- embeddings-service: Availability SLO = 99.5%, p95 latency < 120ms.

Decision matrix (summary):
- Signal: sustained global CPU/GPU usage > 88% for 3m OR p99 latency above SLO OR error_budget_burn_rate > 2.0 for 10m.
- Action tier 1 (early): enable soft attenuation (reduce optional features, prefer quantized model variants).
- Action tier 2 (moderate): apply tenant hedging weights, reduce max tokens for non-critical tenants, increase batching window where latency SLO permits.
- Action tier 3 (severe): enforced preemption of low-priority tokens, model downgrade for low-tier tenants, rolling backlog admission.

Priority hedging policy (example YAML snippet):
---
priority_policy_name: hedged-attenuation-v1
rules:
  - priority: enterprise
    weight: 0.6
    allowed_features: [streaming, function-calls, long_context]
  - priority: standard
    weight: 0.25
    allowed_features: [streaming, function-calls]
  - priority: free
    weight: 0.15
    allowed_features: [short_response, no-function-calls]
---
Notes: weight determines fractional share of available throughput during constrained mode. Implemented as a soft admission controller token-bucket per-tenant group.

Telemetry & dashboards (what to monitor):
- Global capacity: GPU utilization, queue length, active model count, KV cache hit rate.
- SLO signals: success-rate, p50/p95/p99 token latency, error budget remaining by tenant group.
- Attenuation signals: fraction of requests downgraded, model-fallback count, average max_tokens applied.
- Burn-rate alarms: error_budget_burn_rate > 1.25 (warning), > 2.0 (critical).

Runbook: Attenuation activation procedure (engineer-facing)
1) Detect: Confirm sustained constraint (see Decision matrix). Open incident channel with 'attenuation' tag.
2) Assess: Identify impacted clusters, top-consuming tenants (top-20 by QPS/tokens in last 15m), and critical routes. Use CLI: redwood metrics query --top-tenants --window=15m.
3) Early actions (0-5m):
   a) Toggle soft attenuation flag (flags.redwood.runtime.soft_attenuation = true).
   b) Deploy hedging policy 'hedged-attenuation-v1' in policy engine.
   c) Increase batch window from 8ms to 30ms for small requests (if latency SLO allows).
4) Moderate actions (5-15m):
   a) Apply per-tenant max_tokens reduction: default -> 50% for 'free' group.
   b) Prefer quantized model variants for standard/free (model: gptx-quant-1).
   c) Route critical routes to reserved nodes (routing-proxy: --route-critical).
5) Severe actions (15m+):
   a) Execute low-priority preemption: reject non-pinned streaming sessions after 30s.
   b) Evict large KV contexts from cache for low-priority tenants.
   c) If global error budget burn persists, start emergency capacity request to infra and announce degraded mode to customers.
6) Observe: Monitor error budget restoration and latency. Keep attenuation in place only as long as needed.
7) Rollback: Gradually remove measures in reverse order, validating SLO recovery windows (see 'Rollback checklist').

Rollback checklist:
- Confirm sustained error_budget_burn_rate < 1.0 for 30m.
- p99 latency below target for 30m and queue length falling.
- Validate no significant error spikes in customer telemetry for 10m after each step.
- Stepwise re-enable features per priority group: free -> standard -> enterprise.

Incidents & post-incident review triggers:
- Any attenuation window > 60m requires an incident review and SLA impact analysis.
- If more than 5% of requests were downgraded for an enterprise tenant, open customer-impact P0 and notify CS.
- Postmortem should include: timeline of attenuation decisions, top affected tenants, pre/post telemetry for SLOs, and recommended capacity changes.

Incident review standards (what to document):
- Hypothesis and evidence for activation (metrics and thresholds).
- Exact configuration changes (flags, policy id, model variants) with commit SHAs.
- Stakeholders notified and customer-facing comms.
- Root cause: workload spike, memory leak, autoscale failure, or operational misconfiguration.
- Remediation and permanent mitigations (capacity, autoscaler tuning, priority policy refinement).

Operational tooling & automation recommendations:
- Feature flags: integrate attenuation toggles with the feature-flag service and target by tenant-group.
- Policy engine: support staged rollout of priority weights and dry-run reporting.
- Simulation harness: add an "attenuation simulator" to the SLO-sim lab to validate hedging weight effects on p99 and token-cost.
- Observability: add an attenuation-specific panel that shows downgraded requests side-by-side with SLOs and burn rates.
- Playbook endpoints: expose REST hooks to trigger attenuation with RBAC and audit logging. Example CLI: redwood attenuate --policy hedged-attenuation-v1 --dry-run false --reason "excessive-token-spike"

Capacity planning guidance (to avoid frequent attenuation):
- Maintain 15% steady-state headroom for model-serving clusters for 99.9% tenants.
- Reserve 10% dedicated headroom for enterprise-tier guaranteed routes (use Dedicated pools).
- Curate demand profiles per tenant (daily, weekly, 95th, 99th token peaks) and use these to size buffer pools.
- Run monthly "attenuation fire drills": simulate large multi-tenant spikes and validate rollback time < 20min.

Safety & customer experience notes:
- Always prefer reversible, observable measures (reduce max_tokens, prefer lower-fidelity model) over opaque request drops.
- Make degraded mode visible to customers via status page and per-tenant telemetry so they can adapt.
- For enterprise customers, include pre-agreed attenuation terms in the SLA and notify them when hedging is active.

Ownership and escalation:
- Primary owner: model-serving-sre (oncall).
- Secondary: infra-capacity (pager).
- Notify: Customer Success for any enterprise impact, Product for repeated policy triggers, Security if control-plane tokens are affected.

- 2025-11-10: Drafted initial cookbook (Arjun Mehta).

- 2026-02-14: Finalized runbook sequence and rollback checklist; published (Omar Haddad).

Appendix — quick examples:
1) CLI to list top tenants by token usage:
   redwood metrics query --metric tokens_used --group tenant_id --window 15m --limit 20 --format table

2) Sample policy activation curl (audit logged):
   curl -X POST https://policy.redwood.internal/v1/activate \ 
     -H 'Authorization: Bearer $POLICY_KEY' \ 
     -d '{"policy":"hedged-attenuation-v1","reason":"sustained-gpu-constraint"}'

3) Example alert rule (Prometheus pseudo):
   - alert: AttenuationCandidate
     expr: (sum(gpu_utilization) by(cluster) > 0.88) and (increase(error_budget_burn[10m]) > 2)
     for: 5m
     labels: { severity: warning }
     annotations: { runbook: "/confluence/eng-sre/runbooks/attenuation-and-priority-hedging-cookbook-2026" }

Related reading:
- Service-onboarding and SLO admission playbook (link above).
- Tenant SLO and cost playbook for long-term hedging strategies.

If you implement new hedging weights or attenuation strategies, add a follow-up test in the attenuation simulator and schedule a cross-team review with Product and CS.
